text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Romania exported to Germany goods worth 1.5 billion lei last year.
- Romania's army needs 2,000 trucks which it plans to buy from the Roman SA truck maker in Brasov.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Border police in Calafat confiscated 200,000 packages of smuggled cigarattes.
- The Petromin SA state-run shipping company plans to sell 15 ships.
- Heavy snowfalls affected five counties in central and eastern Romania.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Romania's airforce might buy second-hand fighetr jets from the United States, the paper quotes Defence Minister Victor Babiuc as saying.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA

- The prosecution started investigations on alleged forgery, embezzlement and fraud by top businessman George Constantin Paunescu, owner of a tourism and trade holding, police head Pavel Abraham told a news conference.
- Lower Chamber of Deputies' legal commission approved a bank privatisation bill due to be debated on Friday.
- Some 14,000 empoloyees in the farming sector will lose their jobs following cuts in the agriculture ministry budget and plans to liquidate state-run farms.
- Meteorologists estimate that a warm-up of the weather will bring about floods due to the large quantities of snow accumulated in the past days.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Defence Minister Victor Babiuc announced plans to cut 10 percent of jobs in the sector this year.
- Labour protests in the past week have tended to develop in the form of road blockades, the newspaper says.
- Opposition National Unity Party said they will vote against the 1997 budget because none of their amendments was accepted during parliament debates on the budget.
ADEVARUL

- The government will finalise a first set of reform laws for the parliament to discuss next week. The set will include a land leasing law, amendments to a 1991 land restitution law and to banking and bank bankruptcy laws.

- The government will allocate some one trillion lei for compensation to an estimated 200,000 employees who will lose their jobs as a result of restructuring and privatisation, labour ministry officials said.
- The Constitutional Court approved a bill to introduce religion as a compulsory subject matter in schools. ($ = 7,063 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
